thread:
Alex: Heads-up — follow-up on the runtime rollout controls RFC. I pushed a draft for per-model/kernel toggles + fallback policies. Need quick sync on gating, metrics, and rollback rules.

Maria: Nice. Are we using LaunchDarkly or our internal flags service for this? We should prefer the internal store for per-model granularity.

Jon: Agree internal. Proposed key shape: `runtime.kernel.<model_name>`. Example config snippet: 
```yaml
feature_flags:
  runtime:
    kernel:
      gptq-v2:
        enabled: true
        rollout_pct: 10
        fallback: kernel-compat
        auto_fallback: true
```

Kevin: A couple of concerns: 1) Fallbacks must preserve KV cache layout otherwise we flush caches and spike latency. 2) We need memory headroom checks to avoid OOM when switching kernels.

Maria: Good call. Suggest adding a compatibility tag per kernel and a preflight check: `kernel.compatible_with: [kv_cache_v2]`. The rollout system should refuse enabling if compatibility mismatch detected.

Alex: +1. Also want circuit-breaker thresholds: if p95 latency or error rate crosses an SLO, immediate soft-fallback to previous kernel variant. Sample policy: `if p95 > 2s or errors > 1% for 3m -> rollback-automatic`.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for model=gptq-v2 on pool=dedicated-r4. Instances=20 -> rollout=10% :rocket:

Jon: We'll need per-model metrics to evaluate: p50/p95 latency, token throughput, kv_cache_hit_rate, cpu/gpu_util, and memory OOM_count. I can wire dashboards.

Kevin: Also add `kernel_switch_duration` metric so we know how long runtime takes to switch internal kernels (to debug stuck requests).

Maria: For the gating UI, propose a 2D toggle matrix: rows=model versions, cols=kernel variants. Each cell has: enabled(bool), rollout_pct(int), fallback_policy(enum). That maps cleanly to the feature flag shape above.

Alex: How do we handle mixed-mode requests (model pinned to kernel-A but global policy prefers kernel-B)? Priority: per-request override > per-model flag > global default. Documented in RFC follow-ups.

Jon: Implementation note: runtime should evaluate effective kernel at request admission time and tag traces with `kernel.selected` + `kernel.source` (flag/global/override). This helps tracing and postmortem.

Kevin: For rollback, we should implement a fast path: in-flight requests continue on old kernel, new requests go to fallback; then slowly drain old instances. Avoid killing in-flight tensors.

Alex: I'll open INF-983 as post-RFC tracking ticket and include checklist: config schema, console UI, SDK flags, e2e tests, dashboards, rollout playbook, and post-rollout evaluation.

Maria: I'll own console UI + UX for the toggle matrix.

Jon: I'll wire the dashboards and add alerts: alert if p95 jump >20% vs baseline or kv_cache_hit_rate drops >5%.

Kevin: I'll add runtime guards: preflight compatibility and memory headroom check, plus `kernel_switch_duration` instrumentation.

Alex: Action items assigned. Can we aim for a staging canary next week? 

Maria: Yes, aiming for Tue. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Reminder: Add runbook snippet for `kernel_auto_fallback` in incidents playbook.

Alex: Thanks all. I'll update INF-983 with the rollout matrix and link this thread.

Jon: quick Q — do we want automatic cross-model fallbacks (i.e., route to a different model family) or limit to kernel fallbacks only?

Kevin: Limit to kernel fallbacks for initial rollout. Cross-model routing is a separate beast (cost/quality tradeoffs).

Maria: Agreed. Keep initial scope small.

Alex: Cool. I'll post a short RFC follow-up doc today and tag you all on the ticket.

Kevin: LGTM

Maria: Thanks!

Alex: Closing thread for now — will update when INF-983 is created.
